missing_questions.title: Failed Ocean Drown attempt resolves a real Push before cleanup
missing_questions.question: Ocean In Play is active on a board. Infinite Vitality with its threshold protects Dahan in that Ocean, and a Power Pushes a Dahan into it. Ocean In Play triggers but cannot destroy that Dahan. With an adjacent non-Ocean land available, what happens next: does the Dahan remain until cleanup, or is it Pushed? Is that relocation an actual Push within the triggered action or merely cleanup?
missing_questions.predetermined_answer: Ocean In Play Pushes the surviving Dahan to a non-Ocean land as part of its own triggered action. This is an actual Push, capable of triggering applicable movement effects; it is not the later non-action cleanup operation. Cleanup only handles a piece still illegally placed after the action tree. No expansion effect or piece is needed for this branch: the FAQ expressly supplies Infinite Vitality threshold on the Ocean as a core-game case.
missing_questions.why_novel: Q80 asks about Ocean ceasing to be in play when its last Presence is lost; that requires post-tree state cleanup. It never asks what Ocean In Play does when its destruction attempt fails while the Ocean stays active. Q81 asks cleanup classification, not the separate real Push. Q65 asks protection from Remove/Replace and Blight destination legality. Q80 key happens to explain failed Drown Push, but that unrequested sentence earns no coverage credit. This adds the expressly published failed-destruction outcome branch, not the previously rejected Ocean/Vengeance/Bringer recursion recombination.

missing_questions.title: Ordinary Repeat may retarget, including either the same or a different legal land
missing_questions.question: A land-targeting Power Card is Repeated using a permission that does not specify where the Repeat occurs. Must it use the original target land? May it instead use another legal land, and do the ordinary Range and Target restrictions still apply?
missing_questions.predetermined_answer: It need not keep its original target. The Spirit may choose any valid target by the ordinary Range and Target rules, either the original land or a different legal land. Only a Repeat that specifies its destination replaces those normal restrictions with the specified-location instruction.
missing_questions.why_novel: Q43 exclusively tests the specified-adjacent-land exception, including why the original land is forbidden there. It never asks the default no-destination branch, where the original land is allowed and another ordinarily legal target may be selected. The other Repeat prompts test timing, Elements, modifiers, permissions, or counts. This is a distinct choice rule explicitly printed in the book, not a numerical, name, or distance substitution.
